paper.title: Rate-adaptive model selection over a collection of black-box contextual bandit algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection over J base stochastic contextual bandit algorithms
unmapped: Master algorithm combines J black-box base contextual bandit algorithms, each operating over its own policy class Pi_j; regret is measured against the best value over the union of the policy classes
The learner knows the regret-rate exponents beta_j of each base algorithm
Each base algorithm must satisfy an exponential deviation (high-probability) bound on its average conditional regret (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: A master algorithm $\mathcal{M}$ has access to $J$ base contextual bandit algorithms $\mathcal{A}(1),\ldots,\mathcal{A}(J)$. At any time $t$, the master observes a context vector $X(t) \in \mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, selects the index $\widehat{J}(t)$ of a base algorithm, and draws an action $A(t) \in [K]$... We suppose that contexts are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) and that the conditional distribution of rewards given actions and contexts is fixed across time points.

symbols.beta_1: beta(1) = max of beta_j over base algorithms j with optimal limit value V*(E); base algorithm j has regret O~(n^{1-beta_j})
symbols.C_const: constant depending only on the constants of the problem

conditions: Assumption 1: each base algorithm satisfies an exponential deviation bound P[Rbar(j,n) - R*_j >= C_0 n^{-beta_j} + x] <= C_1 exp(-C_2 (n x^{1/beta_j})^{nu_j}) with beta_j <= 1/2
Assumption 2: rewards conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian given the past
tuning: p_t = c_2 t^{-beta_bar} with beta_bar = max_j beta_j
c_1, c_2 constants independent of T

source.label: thm:regret_master
source.quote: Suppose that assumptions \ref{assumption:concentration} and \ref{assumption:conditional_sub_gaussian_rewards} hold, and recall the definition of $\beta(1)$ from subsection \ref{subsection:rate_adaptivity}.  Then, \emph{EnsBFC} is rate-adaptive in pseudo-regret, that is, $$E\left[\sum_{t=1}^T \left(\mathcal{V}^*(\mathcal{E}) - Y(t)\right)\right] \leq C T^{1-\beta(1)},$$ for some $C > 0$ depending only on the constants of the problem.

results.notes: Comparator is V*(E), the best value over the union of the base policy classes. Constant C depends on problem constants including the value gap between suboptimal classes, so it is not purely worst-case. Algorithm does not use T (anytime). Theorem also claims minimax adaptivity when base bounds are minimax. Corollaries 1-3 and Lemma 1 (exponential deviation bounds for UCB, eps-greedy, LinUCB, ILOVETOCONBANDITS) are reformulations of cited results and not recorded as results.
